findings.description: SYS-SUP-022 requires the physical outputs and status signal to reach their specified levels within 50 ms of the detectable instant. SWR-OUT-003 allocates the full 50 ms to the software output write, while OP-SWR-001 assumes an unspecified output-drive delay is negligible. The allocation does not establish that the system deadline can be met.
findings.requested_change: Classify OP-SWR-001 as blocking and establish a software timing allocation that accounts for the output-drive delay.

findings.description: The requirement calls for the last eight fault reports even when fewer than eight exist. OP-SWR-004 leaves the response for that condition undecided, so the expected result cannot be determined after power-on or before eight reports have been recorded.
findings.requested_change: Classify OP-SWR-004 as blocking and define the response when fewer than eight reports exist.

findings.description: The requirement does not identify the event whose time is reported. CON-SUP-126 defines the reset reference and number format, but detection and transmission can occur at different times, so the expected timestamp cannot be determined uniquely.
findings.requested_change: Resolve OP-SWR-006 and specify the event whose elapsed time is reported.

findings.description: SWR-SAF-007 retains elapsed fault-free operation time, but SWR-SAF-009 requires updating the retained values only at fault detection. The set does not require elapsed time to advance during fault-free operation. Its rationale also resets the time at each detection, although SWR-SAF-002 refers to time since the first detection. These gaps prevent reliable application of the repeated-fault rule across resets.
findings.requested_change: Specify how fault-free operation time is updated and how the 60-second condition is evaluated across detections and resets, consistently with SYS-SUP-028.
